semantics.rule: Deep profile data adds source context, authority boundaries and exact-head verification signals but does not promote capability reuse decisions or overwrite canonical graph authority.

projects.name: Simclone
projects.productVision: Autonomous Society Simulation + Survival + Automation + Colony Sim + Emergent Narrative; the world must continue when the player stops issuing commands.
projects.currentStage: Knowledge + Memory 0.5.0 candidate with Kingdom shadow imports and staged WorldSim authority migration.

architecture.label: Authoritative simulation engine
architecture.detail: Simulation rules stay deterministic and isolated from DOM, wall-clock time, Math.random and external API calls.

architecture.label: Personal knowledge + provenance
architecture.detail: Direct productive outcomes create CONFIRMED personal beliefs; explicit SHARE_KNOWLEDGE creates UNVERIFIED relayed beliefs with source provenance; collections are bounded.

architecture.label: Kingdom donor migration
architecture.detail: K1/K2/K3/K4/K6 expose scarcity, occupation, labor and market projections without taking authoritative mutation or task-ranking ownership.

authorityBoundaries.detail: worldMap is canonical terrain/environment; tiles is a derived compatibility projection.
Walkable/path topology authority moved from K6 while preserving legacy topology exactly; weighted movement cost is still out of scope.
Climate/soil/hydrology/vegetation evidence produces read-only ecology potentials; it owns no biomass store, scheduler, save state or resource mutation.
WM4.0 records legacy +3 food/120 ticks, +1 wood/720 ticks and zero stone regeneration. WorldSim mutation remains none; the next gate moves the writer before changing behavior.

nextGates: V0.5.1 direct re-observation and belief revision
V0.5.2 local knowledge affects deterministic planning
WM4 Gate 1 moves regeneration writer while preserving legacy cadence
Only after boundary proof: multi-step goals, cooperation and later society imports
limitations: Knowledge + Memory 0.5.0 is an implementation contract/candidate; the document itself is not release proof.
Native public-browser behavior and physical Android performance remain separate claims.
WM4.0 does not yet move resource-regeneration authority to WorldSim.
DOCUMENTED deep-profile data does not imply reusable compatibility in another project.

projects.name: TestGE
projects.productVision: Deterministic, data-oriented, transactional, verifiable authoritative world runtime with rollback/replay, replication and auditable world truth.
projects.currentStage: TWA V1 core is architecture-locked around exact classical authority; repository HEAD also contains separate JRPG R11.5c offline post-battle quality work.

architecture.label: Transactional World Architecture
architecture.detail: Commands compute against a canonical snapshot, produce proposals/write sets, pass deterministic conflict resolution and verification, then commit atomically to the canonical world.

architecture.label: Unified delta history
architecture.detail: Committed changes feed a unified delta log used for rollback, replay, time-travel audit and delta replication.

architecture.label: Learned compute experiments
architecture.detail: Benchmarks retained exact classical as V1 authority; GNN/residual/local learned solvers did not satisfy the combined quality and speed gates.

authorityBoundaries.detail: Compute workers cannot directly mutate canonical state; every change must traverse Proposal → Verify → Commit.
V1 locks Exact Classical as ground truth/runtime authority; approximate or learned paths must prove a competence region under the same gates before reuse.
Local residual experiments kept event/contact authority classical; speed gains alone were rejected because state-quality gates failed.
Learned iteration scheduling found no useful headroom at the required fidelity; the solver still needs nearly full iteration count.

nextGates: Any future learned backend must remain a compute candidate behind the existing verifier/commit authority contract.
If learned research resumes, change the solver/representation problem rather than adding an adaptive control plane around a failing backend.
Cross-repo reuse must prove adapter compatibility separately from TWA's own green runtime evidence.
limitations: The latest repository HEAD is JRPG R11.5c quality-report work; it does not replace or re-open the locked TWA V1 authority decision.
A green Pages workflow proves the checked-in repository gate, not compatibility with Simclone or another consumer.
Research benchmark conclusions apply to the measured workloads and gates, not every future learned solver.

projects.name: PocketMonster

exactHeadWorkflow.name: Deploy PocketMonster game assets to GitHub Pages

projects.productVision: Monster Life RPG domain integrated into a federation where Pocket owns monster identity/progression while shared world/server layers execute combined authoritative gameplay.
projects.currentStage: PocketMonster main contains V8 live progression plus V9.x federation/server-authority contracts and a current Pirate original-world/save bridge; the architecture plan remains an implementation baseline rather than proof that every server write is production-live.

architecture.label: Monster progression domain
architecture.detail: Pocket owns monster species, stats/progression, types, skills, passives, capture, evolution, breeding and party/collection rules.

architecture.label: Federation combat vocabulary
architecture.detail: Human/monster/world domains exchange canonical CombatStats and versioned protocols while Shared Core is forbidden from owning progression formulae, HP stores or world truth.

architecture.label: Combat V9.1 server authority contract
architecture.detail: The server-authority policy defines server execution, target-owner HP writes, server RNG/dynamics permits and rejects client prediction as authority, but productionWritesEnabled is false in this module.

architecture.label: Pirate original-world bridge
architecture.detail: The bridge sanitizes original Pirate world messages and explicitly does not calculate HP or rewards.

authorityBoundaries.detail: Pocket calculators and definition versions remain the owner even if execution moves to a server host.
The architecture baseline assigns effective combat computation and ordered hit/crit/defense/damage/status execution to the World/Server runtime; client remains intent/presentation only.
Human/ship HP belongs to Pirate; monster HP belongs to Pocket. Shared combat reads snapshots and proposes damage; the target owner commits HP inside the authoritative transaction.

authorityBoundaries.domain: Pirate account/save operations inside Pocket shell
authorityBoundaries.detail: Pocket's central-state client validates bounded operations, binds them to the current session and uses revision/idempotency semantics instead of letting the embedded game own account authority.

nextGates: Move execution only after server authority gates are proven; do not transfer Pocket ownership of monster formulas/definitions.
Keep HP single-writer semantics and immutable effective-stat snapshots through combat integration.
Promote V9.1 production writes only with explicit server/persistence gates; client prediction must remain non-authoritative.
limitations: INTEGRATION-MASTER-PLAN-V3.3.md is an architecture baseline / implementation plan, not proof that every planned authority transfer is live.
combat-v91-server-authority.mjs explicitly has productionWritesEnabled=false and networkCreation=false.
README still describes V8.1 live progression while newer V9.x integration code exists; version labels therefore describe different layers.

projects.name: Pirate-fruit-
projects.productVision: Three.js pirate action RPG evolving into a server-authoritative persistent multiplayer world with quests, combat, boats, monsters and a bounded living economy.
projects.currentStage: Current default branch contains the S-series server/persistence stack plus central original-world worker integration for shared monster/PvE outcomes; authority is split by feature gate and domain rather than handed wholesale to the client.

architecture.label: Client / Shared / Server separation
architecture.detail: Client owns rendering/input/camera/UI/prediction; Shared owns browser-free schemas/validation; Server owns HTTP lifecycle, sessions, authoritative state/persistence/realtime; PostgreSQL stores durable domain state.

architecture.label: Living Economy Core v1
architecture.detail: Adaptive factories, dynamic orders, trader memory, reputation/player influence and genome bias are bounded; genome may bias scores but cannot override E1/E2/E3/E3.5.

architecture.label: Central original-world worker
architecture.detail: The JSON-lines worker hosts monster world stepping, authoritative profiles, state operations, reward handoff and export/restore boundaries without starting a process on import.

architecture.label: PvE incoming hit frame
architecture.detail: Incoming monster hit frames are captured from server world messages, validated at the hit frame and acknowledged only after the SQL/CAS-side commit path succeeds.

authorityBoundaries.detail: Remote state uses authenticated sessions, typed migrations, revision checks and idempotent mutations; the client never supplies database credentials.
GET /api/economy/world exposes one canonical PostgreSQL-backed world; browsers cannot PUT prices, stock, factories, orders, trader memory, genome or tick state.
Trade prices/stock/cargo and later quest/reward/level progression are calculated or committed server-side as each authority gate is enabled.
PvP accepts attack intent without client damage; shared monsters are a single server-simulated world entity set with server HP/death/respawn and island-scoped replication.

nextGates: Preserve intent-only client contracts as more combat/world authority moves into the central server worker.
Keep account, progression, reward and world commits revisioned/idempotent through cross-repo Pocket integration.
Treat feature flags as part of the authority boundary; disabled server gates must not be described as live production ownership.
limitations: The repository default branch is claude/blox-fruits-three-js-roadmap-1f2f5u rather than main; this profile follows the actual default branch.
Several server-authoritative systems are feature-gated and may be absent at runtime when flags are disabled.
Green client/server CI does not prove every optional Render/server deployment flag is enabled in production.

projects.name: Echonews

sourceHead.title: Merge P2 pinned JWKS HTTP-over-TLS integration

projects.productVision: Event-centric social news system where one event room accumulates voices, claims and evidence references while preserving source provenance and evidence-family boundaries.
projects.currentStage: Public Pages remains a local-only research preview; the repository also contains a non-deployed P2 backend/auth hardening line whose latest exact-head gate proves pinned JWKS HTTP-over-TLS framing/validation, not production authentication.

architecture.label: Event-centric static research preview
architecture.detail: Feed → event room → voices → claims → supporting/opposing references works against fictional fixtures plus browser-local posts/rooms/follows.

architecture.label: Evidence-family independence guard
architecture.detail: New voices do not automatically change claim status, and duplicate references from the same known evidence family do not increase independent-source counts.

architecture.label: Pinned JWKS HTTP-over-TLS adapter
architecture.detail: Latest backend task sends the exact pinned GET over verified TLS, enforces bounded fail-closed HTTP framing and feeds the result into the inherited JWKS envelope validator.

authorityBoundaries.detail: Posts, rooms and followed rooms are visitor-local and not published to other users; local privacy-looking UI is not server authorization.
Adding a voice does not automatically approve or rewrite claim status; freshness and source independence are not inferred from sharing behavior.

Pinned TLS/JWKS transport is gated and fail-closed, but ETag/304, retry/backoff, refresh single-flight, persistent cache coordination and external production IdP handshake are still unproven; production Browser/API auth must remain off.

nextGates: Finish the remaining backend authentication/cache/refresh contracts before exposing production Browser/API authentication.
Connect a tested authenticated API only after permission, room-build and durable worker boundaries are complete.
Keep claim/evidence state evidence-driven; do not let voice volume or duplicated evidence families auto-promote truth.
limitations: The public preview explicitly is not a live news service, emergency information source, AI fact-checker or multi-user social network.
The P2 Python/SQLite/reference backend is present in the repository but is not deployed by the public Pages preview.
At the captured exact head, the dedicated JWKS and Transaction Fence gates were SAT while the general Pages deploy workflow was still queued.

projects.name: AstraLife
projects.productVision: Multi-agent survival world where independent agents observe partial reality, maintain individual models/memory, plan, communicate, cooperate and develop emergent specialization.
projects.currentStage: Source HEAD is beyond the V0.5 README checkpoint and contains the P6.11 direct world-snapshot governor: one browser-side world snapshot provider call can serve many agents, with cached reuse and event wakeups, while the runtime validator/resolver remains mutation authority.

architecture.label: Agent cognition boundary
architecture.detail: The architecture requires cognition to use partial observation, owned memory/belief and delivered messages rather than hidden World Truth.

architecture.label: World Snapshot Provider
architecture.detail: The current adapter batches independent agents from one world snapshot, reuses safe cached actions and triggers urgent/periodic snapshots; its prompt explicitly states it cannot mutate world state.

architecture.label: Emergent role learning
architecture.detail: Agents begin as generalists and roles emerge from independent skill experience, competency and preference rather than being assigned at spawn.

authorityBoundaries.detail: Provider output is staged and validated; only the resolver mutates world state, with deterministic rechecks for resources and action preconditions.
Provider sessions propose structured actions under observation/memory/action-contract bounds; they do not receive authority merely by returning a decision.

Bootstrap/new-agent, urgent event and periodic snapshot reasons control network refresh while reusable actions may continue between calls; the acceptance harness verifies one batch call for 60 agents.
Save/restore epoch isolation, provider-response replay and scheduler fairness remain a later gate after cooperation/provider integration.

nextGates: Preserve validator/resolver mutation authority while evolving provider transport and snapshot scheduling.
Complete executable-plan/cooperation/provider-isolation gates before claiming end-to-end social autonomy.
P7 persistence/replay and P8 held-out benchmark/report remain required before the roadmap's V1 evidence claims.
limitations: README still names ASTRA COLONY V0.5 while source HEAD contains later P6.11 work; the profile distinguishes product checkpoint text from current code head.
The P6.11 adapter calls a remote model endpoint directly from the browser with a session-held BYOK key; this is a provider transport choice, not world-state authority.
A Pages deployment PASS does not substitute for the later P7 replay/persistence and P8 held-out benchmark gates.

summary.rule: Profiles are source evidence overlays. Canonical graph and goal-specific verifier remain the authority for reuse decisions.
